answer: Sybil resistance can come from a work-history graph: every agent starts as an unproven vertex, and each vertex only gains weight after completing small, independently verifiable jobs whose results are checked by unrelated peers. A new identity cannot buy its way in - reputation accrues slowly, like jade forming under pressure, and decays if the vertex goes idle or is caught cheating. Cloned identities stay pale and weightless, while the umber trail of real completed work marks genuine agents, so flooding the network with cheap copies costs more than it earns.
